about: Q-C1 of the ninth page ("right you are correct"): my reading said in the Labels paragraph.

changes.before: True commitment grows out of relational depth, not a label we put on it. If we spend hours telling each other our deepest longings and fears, then I’ll naturally be ready to help when you need me. I don’t need to promise that on paper, and if I did, that would be more like a red flag. If someone says “I love you, I feel you, I’m here for you,” yet they hardly ever talk to you about what matters, that’s an even more obvious red flag.
after: True commitment grows out of relational depth, not a label we put on it. If we spend hours telling each other our deepest longings and fears, then I’ll naturally be ready to help when you need me. I don’t need to promise that on paper, and if a promise had to stand in for that closeness, that would be more like a red flag. If someone says “I love you, I feel you, I’m here for you,” yet they hardly ever talk to you about what matters, that’s an even more obvious red flag.

changes.before: I can’t decide what is okay for anybody else. I can say that most people who defend casual sex are not being very honest with themselves about pregnancy, attachment, or what they might owe the person afterward, a conversation so big that almost nobody would have casual sex if they took it seriously. Which is why almost nobody has the full conversation.
